newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tietmeyer hopes dollar correction has now ended.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer hopes dollar correction has now ended.

text.p: Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer was quoted on Wednesday as saying the dollar's recent rise against the mark was "a normalisation of exchange rates which has been due for a long time".
But he also told the mass-circulation Bild newspaper, according to an advance release of Wednesday morning's edition, that he hoped this correction had now ended.
The dollar hit a 34-month high of 1.7050 marks in European trade on Tuesday.
Tietmeyer was also quoted by the newspaper as saying current interest rate levels were not an obstacle to economic growth or jobs, but that he would not rule out further cuts.
In Tokyo the dollar fell sharply against mark in reaction to Tietmeyer's comments that the dollar rise was an overdue correction. At 0200 GMT the dollar-mark was quoted at 1.6850/55.
Overnight, the dollar fell from its nearly three-year high against the mark as the mark was bolstered by precipitous falls in both the Italian lira and British pound.
